passages.text: Knowing these things beforehand about Appion, as soon as he asked the cause of my illness, I answered in pretense, “I suffer what young men suffer, and my soul aches.” He replied, “Child, trust me as you would a father and tell me: what is the illness of your soul?” Once again I sighed in pretense, as though ashamed to speak about being in love. By my silence and by lowering my head, I gave him grounds to suspect what I wanted to suggest. Convinced that I was truly in love with a woman, he said, “There is nothing in life that cannot receive help. For when I myself was young, I fell in love with a most distinguished woman. Not only did I consider it impossible to obtain her; I did not even hope ever to address her. Nevertheless, I happened to meet an Egyptian who was highly accomplished in the practices of magicians. After he befriended me, I disclosed my passion, and he not only placed himself at my disposal for everything I wanted, but, endeavoring to be even more lavish toward me, did not begrudge teaching me also the incantation through which I obtained her. Persuaded by that secret instruction of his and by the unstinting generosity of the man who taught me, after I had succeeded once, I stopped being in love.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: I suffer what young men suffer
lexical_decisions.rationale: The compact expression literally refers to “the things of young men.” The rendering preserves Appion’s intended inference of youthful erotic distress without adding it directly to Clement’s words.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: διά γε τῆς σιωπῆς καὶ τοῦ κάτω νεύειν
lexical_decisions.chosen: By my silence and by lowering my head
lexical_decisions.rationale: κάτω νεύειν describes the visible gesture of inclining or lowering the head, here conveying affected embarrassment.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὁ δὲ ἐρᾶν με γυναικὸς ἀληθῶς ἀναπεισθεὶς ἔφη
lexical_decisions.chosen: Convinced that I was truly in love with a woman, he said
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀληθῶς can qualify either ἐρᾶν (“truly in love”) or ἀναπεισθείς (“truly convinced”). The main rendering attaches it to the supposed love because Appion interprets Clement’s affected behavior as evidence of a real passion; the alternative is “Truly convinced that I was in love with a woman.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐ μόνον αὐτῆς τυχεῖν ἡγούμην ἀδύνατον εἶναι, ἀλλ’ οὐδὲ προσαγορεῦσαί ποτε ἤλπιζον
lexical_decisions.chosen: Not only did I consider it impossible to obtain her; I did not even hope ever to address her
lexical_decisions.rationale: The coordinated clauses express an escalation from regarding possession of her as impossible to lacking even the hope of ever speaking to her.

lexical_decisions.chosen: highly accomplished in the practices of magicians
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀκριβόω here signifies exact mastery or thorough knowledge; τὰ μάγων denotes the matters or practices belonging to magicians.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ φιλωθεὶς ἐκφαίνω μου τὸν ἔρωτα
lexical_decisions.chosen: After he befriended me, I disclosed my passion
lexical_decisions.rationale: The passive φιλωθείς can mean being loved or treated as a friend. “Befriended” fits the ensuing disclosure, while ἐκφαίνω is represented according to the sense of its vivid historical present.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the incantation through which I obtained her
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἐπαοιδή is a sung spell or incantation. Although the object of ἔτυχον is implicit here, the earlier αὐτῆς τυχεῖν supplies the woman as its contextual object; an alternative is “through which I succeeded.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐκ δὲ τῆς ἐκείνου λαθραίας ὑποδείξεως πεισθεὶς τῇ τοῦ διδάξαντος ἀφθονίᾳ
lexical_decisions.chosen: Persuaded by that secret instruction of his and by the unstinting generosity of the man who taught me
lexical_decisions.rationale: The dative τῇ … ἀφθονίᾳ is taken instrumentally alongside ἐκ τῆς … ὑποδείξεως. An alternative is “persuaded by that secret instruction of his to trust in the teacher’s unstinting generosity.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ ἅπαξ ἐπιτυχών, ἐπαυσάμην τοῦ ἔρωτος
lexical_decisions.chosen: after I had succeeded once, I stopped being in love
lexical_decisions.rationale: Placing “once” after “succeeded” explicitly preserves the numerical force of ἅπαξ rather than reducing it to a temporal conjunction meaning merely “after.”

source_issues.issue: The confirmed print has μὲ with a grave accent. The context provisionally supports understanding it as the pronoun με, “me,” rather than as an incomplete μέν; the proposed reading regularizes the accent but is not the supplied text.
